paragraphs.en: Try to finish with a higher total than the dealer without going over 21. Number cards count as shown, face cards are worth ten, and an ace counts as eleven if that fits, otherwise as one. You play with virtual chips.
Each player pays an opening stake, normally ten chips. If you cannot cover the table’s opening stake, you put in what you have. Players then bet in turn.
Press C to check if you owe nothing or call to match the bet. F folds: you leave the round and give up what you have paid. A puts in all your chips. You stay in the round but cannot bet again.

To raise, press R and enter how much higher the bet should be. Any amount you need to call is added to your payment. The first raise is at least one chip; later raises must match the last full raise. A smaller all-in does not let a player who already acted raise again unless the smaller increases together make a full raise.
Betting ends when one player remains or everyone still in the round with chips has responded and matched the bet.

After betting, you get two cards and see one of the dealer’s. Press H to hear your cards and their total. On your turn, press Space to draw a card, or choose Keep your total in the actions list and press Enter. Your turn ends automatically at 21 or above.

After the players finish, the dealer reveals the second card. The dealer draws below 17 and stops on 17 or above, even with an ace counted as eleven. If the dealer starts with 21, the round is settled immediately.

Going over 21 loses the bet, even if the dealer goes over too. Otherwise you win if the dealer goes over or has a lower total. An ordinary win returns the stake and pays the same amount in profit; equal totals return the stake.
An opening total of 21 from two cards is blackjack. It beats an ordinary 21 and pays three chips in profit for every two staked. If you and the dealer both have blackjack, you get your stake back.

title.en: End of the match and extended play

paragraphs.en: After the last round, the highest chip balance wins. Equal highest balances draw. The default is ten rounds and 100 starting chips. The match ends early if nobody has chips left.

In the extended game, choose Double down in the actions list to double your stake and take exactly one card. A pair of the same rank can also be split into two hands by adding a second stake. Play those hands separately. Neither can be split or doubled again; split aces get one card each. A split hand does not pay the blackjack bonus.
There is no dealer hand. After betting, the player who is dealing presses D, then plays their own hand last. The dealing seat changes each round. There is no doubling, splitting or blackjack bonus.

The highest total up to 21 wins the pot; tied players split it. A player with a smaller stake can only win as much from each other player as they put in themselves. If all players eligible for a pot go over 21, the bets in that pot are returned.
Space: draw a card
H: read your cards and total
S: read chip balances
T: read the current turn
C: check or call
F: fold in betting
A: go all-in
R: raise
B: raise
D: deal in social blackjack
